title: How do you write a training policy?
description: How to write a training policy for a regulated organization: purpose, scope, obligations, roles, mandatory training, assessment, records, and review.
shortAnswer: To write a training policy, state its purpose and scope, list the obligations it supports, assign roles and accountabilities, set how training needs are identified, define mandatory training and timeframes, state how competence is assessed, set record keeping and retention rules, cover non completion, content governance, and evaluation, then have it approved at the right level and reviewed on a fixed cycle. Keep procedures and schedules in separate, linked documents.
keyTakeaways: A training policy sets principles, accountabilities, and minimum standards. Detailed steps belong in procedures.
Anchor the policy in the obligations that apply to you, such as anti money laundering rules, workplace safety duties, or sector rules on personnel training.
Define who decides what training each role needs, and how competence, not just completion, is confirmed.
Record keeping, retention, and version control rules should be explicit, because they decide what you can prove later.
Set an approval owner and a review cycle, and review the policy after any major regulatory change.

sections.heading: What is the difference between a training policy and a procedure?

blocks.text: A training policy states what the organization commits to and who is accountable; a procedure states how the work is done step by step. Keeping them separate lets procedures change without reapproving the policy, and makes the policy readable by the board and regulators.

Some regimes make the policy itself an obligation. In the European Union, the [Anti-Money Laundering Regulation (EU) 2024/1624](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1624/oj/eng) requires obliged entities to have internal policies that include a policy on the training of employees and, where relevant, agents and distributors, approved by the management body (Article 9). Australia's AML/CTF regulator, AUSTRAC, [states](https://www.austrac.gov.au/about-us/amlctf-reform/reforms-guidance/amlctf-program-reform/personnel-due-diligence-and-training-reform/amlctf-training-reform), referring to Rules section 5 to 9(2) and (3), that AML/CTF policies must ensure initial and ongoing training for personnel who perform AML/CTF functions, and expects those policies to outline a training plan, a register of completion dates, and monitoring of training effectiveness.

sections.heading: Which obligations should the policy be anchored to?

blocks.text: Anchor the policy to every obligation that requires training, competence, or records in your organization, and cite each one. The anchors below are examples from different sectors and jurisdictions; yours will depend on where you operate.

items: **Medicines manufacturing.** In the United States, 21 CFR 211.25(a) requires that each person engaged in manufacturing, processing, packing, or holding a drug product has the education, training, and experience to perform their assigned functions, with good manufacturing practice training "conducted by qualified individuals on a continuing basis and with sufficient frequency" ([21 CFR 211.25](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-211/subpart-B/section-211.25)).

**Anti money laundering (United States).** The Bank Secrecy Act requires an ongoing employee training program as one element of an AML program (31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(1)(C)), and FinCEN's rules for banks require training for appropriate personnel ([31 CFR 1020.210](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-31/subtitle-B/chapter-X/part-1020/subpart-B/section-1020.210)). See [BSA AML training requirements](/regulations/bsa-aml-training-requirements).

**Anti money laundering (European Union).** Article 12 of the EU [Anti-Money Laundering Regulation](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1624/oj/eng), which applies from July 10, 2027, requires specific, ongoing, and documented training programs. See [EU AMLR training requirements](/regulations/eu-amlr-training-requirements).

**Continuous training (Portugal).** Article 131(2) of the Portuguese Labor Code entitles each worker to a minimum of 40 hours of continuous training per year ([Labor Code](https://diariodarepublica.pt/dr/legislacao-consolidada/lei/2009-34546475)). See [Portugal Labor Code continuous training](/regulations/portugal-labour-code-continuous-training).

**Occupational safety and health (European Union and Japan).** Article 12 of the [OSH Framework Directive 89/391/EEC](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31989L0391) requires adequate, job specific safety training on recruitment, change of job, and new equipment or technology. Japan's [Industrial Safety and Health Act](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/347AC0000000057) requires safety or health education on hiring and on a change of work content (Article 59).

**Quality management.** Organizations using ISO based management systems may also align with [ISO 10015:2019](https://www.iso.org/standard/69459.html), which gives guidelines for competence management and people development.

sections.heading: What is the step by step method?

items: **List obligations.** Extract every training, competence, and record requirement from your [compliance obligations register](/glossary/compliance-obligations-register). Output: an obligations list with citations.
**Agree accountabilities.** Decide who owns the policy, who decides role requirements, who approves content, and who monitors compliance. Output: a roles table.
**Draft the sections.** Use the checklist below. Output: a first draft.
**Test against real cases.** Walk three scenarios through the draft: a new starter in a high risk role, a regulatory change, and a person who does not complete training. Output: a list of gaps fixed.
**Consult.** Seek input from compliance, legal, HR, operations, and worker representatives where consultation is required. Output: a consultation record.
**Approve and publish.** Approve at the level your governance framework requires and publish with an effective date. Output: the approved policy.
**Implement procedures.** Write or update the procedures and schedules the policy refers to. Output: linked procedures.

sections.heading: What sections should a training policy contain?

blocks.text: The checklist below is original and covers the sections most regulated organizations need. Not every row applies to every organization.

blocks.caption: Training policy section checklist
head: Section
What to include
Why it matters
rows: Purpose and scope
Who the policy covers, including contractors and volunteers where relevant
Coverage gaps often start with unclear scope
Obligations
The laws, standards, and internal policies the training supports, with citations
Shows the policy is grounded in actual requirements
Roles and responsibilities
Policy owner, role requirement owners, content approvers, managers, workers
Makes accountability auditable
Needs identification
How training needs are set for each role, and when they are reviewed
Links training to risk and role; see [how to conduct a training needs analysis](/guides/how-to-conduct-a-training-needs-analysis)
Mandatory training
Categories, timeframes for new starters and role changes, refresher cycles
Sets the standard that records are tested against
Competence and assessment
How competence is confirmed, including assessment and verification of competency where relevant
Distinguishes completion from competence; see [how to set up verification of competency](/guides/how-to-set-up-verification-of-competency)
Records and retention
Required record fields, systems of record, retention periods, version tracking
Decides what can be proven later
Non completion and exemptions
Escalation steps, consequences, who can grant exemptions and how they are recorded
Prevents silent gaps
Content governance
Ownership, approval, version control, review, and response to regulatory change
Keeps content accurate and current
Evaluation and reporting
How effectiveness is measured and what is reported to executives and the board
Supports oversight duties
Review
Review cycle and triggers, approval authority
Keeps the policy current

sections.heading: What does policy wording look like?

blocks.text: Policy wording should be short, specific, and testable, so an auditor can check whether it was followed.

blocks.title: Illustrative sample clauses, adapt before use
blocks.text: 1. Each role in scope has a documented training requirement, set by the role owner with compliance and reviewed at least annually and after any material regulatory change. 2. Workers complete role specific mandatory training within the timeframe stated in the training schedule, and before performing the relevant function unsupervised. 3. Competence for high risk functions is confirmed by assessment against defined criteria; completion alone does not satisfy this clause. 4. Training records include the content version completed and the assessment outcome, and are retained for the period in the records schedule. 5. Exemptions are approved in writing by the compliance manager and recorded with the reason.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry gives a training policy something concrete to point to: a framework that links obligations, role requirements, learning outcomes, and assessment points with their sources. Policy clauses on needs identification, competence, and content governance can then refer to that structure.

faqs.q: How long should a training policy be?
faqs.a: Long enough to state commitments, accountabilities, and minimum standards, and no longer. Many workable policies fit in a few pages, with detail moved into procedures, schedules, and the training matrix. A policy nobody reads is not followed.

faqs.q: Who should approve the training policy?
faqs.a: Whoever your governance framework assigns to approve policies of that significance, often an executive committee, with board or committee oversight where training supports material obligations. The policy should name its owner and approver.

faqs.q: Does a training policy need to name specific courses?
faqs.a: No. Name categories and link to a schedule or training matrix that lists current items. That way courses can change without the policy being reapproved.

faqs.q: How often should a training policy be reviewed?
faqs.a: Set a fixed cycle, commonly annual or biennial, and add triggers such as a material regulatory change, a significant incident, a merger, or an audit finding. Regulator expectations that training reflects regulatory change, such as those of Japan's Financial Services Agency (FSA), are a reminder that the policy's content governance section must work between reviews.
